How Solar Panels Work

By Jane Doe, March 3 2024

Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity using photovoltaic cells made of silicon. When photons strike the cell, they knock electrons loose, creating a flow of current that can power homes and businesses.

Efficiency

Modern residential panels typically reach an efficiency between 18 and 23 percent, while laboratory cells have exceeded 47 percent using multi-junction designs that stack several materials together.

Panel typeEfficiencyCost per watt
Monocrystalline20-23%$1.00
Polycrystalline15-18%$0.80

Installing them

Installation usually takes one to three days. The steps are:

  1. Site survey and shading analysis of the roof
  2. Mounting the racking system to the rafters
  3. Wiring the inverter and connecting to the grid
def output(kw, hours):

Most systems pay for themselves within six to ten years depending on local electricity prices and incentives available in your region.
